catalog_quote: Stress and intonation interact but function on different levels. Stress is mostly a lexical feature in Dameli and serves to differentiate between word forms, whereas intonation is used to mark particular sentence types and perform discourse functions. ... 5.1 Stress ... Stress is mainly lexically determined and can fall on any syllable. Some suffixes carry their own stress, altering the stress of the word they form part of. This is particularly true for verb endings, which often change the stress pattern considerably. Stress and long vowels mostly coincide, although it is often impossible to determine whether the long vowel attracted the stress or the stress caused vowel lengthening. There are, however, enough examples of words with long, unstressed vowels, or several long vowels, to warrant positing length and stress as independent features. audit.reasoning: The classification (lexical stress, any syllable, morphologically perturbed by stressed suffixes, length only a tendency) rests on the sole reference grammar of Dameli (Perder 2013, 242 pp), which we hold as the genuine DiVA diva2:651418 FULLTEXT02 PDF (the earlier wrong diva2:604657 fetch is documented as deleted). Every quoted sentence was found verbatim at the stated pages (p. 36 ch. 5/5.1; p. 26; p. 32). No newer or more specialised stress/prosody study of Dameli exists per Glottolog and web search; the remaining literature is a 1942 sketch, a 4-page 2003 handbook sketch and a 2014 areal survey, none likely to alter the coding. One optional refinement for the caution field, already visible in the held source: Dameli also has an under-analysed rising vs falling tone contrast (Perder 3.3, citing Morgenstierne 1942:125 and Strand 2001, who limits tone to accented vowels)
